title_screening: Malnutrition and mortality risk among older adult patients with cancer in Peru. [Spanish]
abstract: Objective: Malnutrition is common among cancer patients and even more prevalent in older adults. Although its association with mortality risk is well established, further studies in Latin America are needed to delve deeper into this relationship. This study aimed to evaluate the association between malnutrition and mortality risk among Peruvian older adult patients (>= 60 years) with cancer. Material(s) and Method(s): Comprehensive geriatric assessment (CGA) records of older adult patients with cancer evaluated at the Geriatrics Department of Hospital Almenara in Lima, Peru, from 2018 to January 2024, were reviewed. Nutritional status was assessed using the Mini Nutritional Assessment Short Form (MNA-SF), which classifies patients into three groups: normal, at risk of malnutrition, or malnourished. This retrospective observational study comprised both cases (patients at risk of malnutrition or malnourished) and controls. Result(s): The study included 171 patients (mean age of 77.8 +/- 7.5 years), 60 % of whom were men. According to the MNA-SF, 66 patients (38.5 %) were classified as having normal nutritional status, 77 (45.0 %) as at risk of malnutrition, and 28 (16.4 %) as malnourished. The frequency of malnutrition was higher among males (60.7 %) than females (39.3 %) (p < 0.05). The mean follow-up period was 41.1 +/- 20.9 months, ranging from 0.9 to 68 months. The most common cancer types were colorectal (23.4 %), prostate (13.5 %), stomach (11.7 %), skin (11.7 %), breast (9.4 %), non-Hodgkin lymphoma (5.4 %), head and neck (4.7 %), lung (3.5 %), endometrial (3.5 %), and pancreatic (2.9 %). In the multivariate Cox regression analysis, patients who were at risk of malnutrition or malnourished had a higher mortality risk compared to those with normal nutritional status (hazard ratio [HR], 2.9; 95 % confidence interval [CI], 1.37-7.26; p < 0.01). Conclusion(s): Peruvian older adult patients with cancer at risk of malnutrition or malnourished have a higher mortality risk compared with their counterparts with normal nutritional status. title_screening: Prevalence of Tuberculosis and Related Factors Among Malnourished Under-Five Children in a Therapeutic Feeding Centre, Specialist Hospital, Sokoto, Nigeria
abstract: Background: Tuberculosis (TB) is a chronic infectious disease caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, primarily affecting the respiratory system but can disseminate to other organs including the CNS, bones, and lymph nodes. TB and malnutrition are leading causes of childhood morbidity and mortality in low-income countries. With TB accounting for 11% of the 9 million new infections in children each year, while malnutrition is responsible for the deaths of approximately 2.2 million children under the age of five globally. This study aimed to assess the prevalence of TB in children with severe acute malnutrition (SAM) and identify associated factors among under-five children admitted to the In-Patient Therapeutic Feeding Center (ITFC) at Specialist Hospital Sokoto (SHS), Sokoto State. Material(s) and Method(s): A cross-sectional study was conducted using consecutive sampling among 146 under-five children with severe acute malnutrition (SAM) at the ITFC, SHS, between July and August 2024. Data were obtained from patient records and through an interviewer-administered questionnaire using Open Data Kit (ODK), and analysed with IBM SPSS version 26. Result(s): Among the 146 participants included in this study, most participants were aged 6-42 months, with a mean age of 17.14 months +/- 7.0 SD. The prevalence of TB in the study was 5.5%. No statistically significant associations were found between TB and factors such as age, sex, low economic status, vaccination, exclusive breastfeeding, HIV infection, or place of residence (p > 0.05). Conclusion(s): This study revealed a prevalence of TB among malnourished under-five children admitted in ITFC, however, no statistically significant associations were found between TB and any specific factors. In general, Strengthening integrated TB prevention, screening, and nutritional rehabilitation strategies is recommended for timely detection and decrease the overall burden of childhood TB and paediatric malnutrition in this vulnerable population in Nigeria. title_screening: Clinical phenotypes of patients receiving 3-in-1 parenteral nutrition in a national hospital in Peru: A cluster analysis
abstract: Rationale: We aimed to identify distinct clinical profiles among patients receiving 3-in-1 parenteral nutrition (PN). Method(s): A retrospective multivariate observational study was conducted on 116 hospitalized patients who received 3-in-1 PN during 2024 at a national hospital in Peru. Variables analyzed included sex, age, hospital ward, nutritional diagnosis, PN duration, renal failure, and in-hospital mortality. A hierarchical cluster analysis was performed using Ward's method and squared Euclidean distance. Four optimal clusters were identified from the dendrogram. Result(s): The mean age was 56.3 years (SD +/-17.9), with 58.6% males. Half were admitted to the ICU. Indications were intestinal failure (86.2%) and gastrointestinal tract injury (13.8%). Mean PN duration was 11 days (SD +/-10.65). Renal failure occurred in 23.3% and mortality was 29.3%. Cluster 1 included critically ill patients with high mortality (74.2%) and renal failure (77.4%).Cluster 2 comprised only stable male patients with no organ failure or deaths. Cluster 3 included females with intermediate risk and 27.8% mortality but no organ dysfunction. Cluster 4 involved patients with intestinal injury, low mortality (6.3%), and variable outcomes. These profiles reflected different clinical and nutritional risk levels. Conclusion(s): Hierarchical cluster analysis enabled the identification of four distinct clinical phenotypes among patients receiving parenteral nutrition. References: Cederholm, T., & Jensen, G. L. (2021). Assessment of malnutrition in clinical settings. In J. M. Kinney & H. R. Feibelman (Eds.), Nutrition in Clinical Practice (3rd ed., pp. 112-125). Elsevier. title_screening: The health, environmental, and cost implications of providing healthy and sustainable school meals for every child by 2030: a global modelling study
abstract: BACKGROUND: School meal programmes are thought to improve dietary behaviour in children, with benefits sustained throughout the life course, making them important catalysts for wider food-system change. However, only one in five children globally currently receives school meals. We estimated the potential effects of extending school meal coverage to all children by 2030 for dietary health; the environmental effects related to diets; and the costs of diets at global, regional, and national levels. METHOD(S): We conducted health, environmental, and cost assessments of future scenarios of school meal coverage, meal frequency, meal composition, and food wastage. In the health assessment, we used statistical methods and a comparative risk assessment to estimate short-term changes in undernourishment and long-term changes in dietary risks and mortality. In the environmental assessment, we used food-related environmental footprints to analyse how changes in dietary composition and food waste affect greenhouse gas emissions, land use, and freshwater use. In the cost assessment, we used an international dataset of food prices to estimate changes in diet costs, and we used estimates of the social cost of carbon and the costs of illness to estimate changes in the costs of climate-change damages and in health-related costs. FINDINGS: Extending school meal programmes to all children globally by 2030 could be associated with substantial health and environmental benefits globally and in each country. In the model assessments, the prevalence of undernourishment in food-insecure populations was reduced by a quarter due to having an additional meal at school; more than 1 million cases of non-communicable diseases were prevented globally per year if dietary habits were partly sustained into adulthood; and food-related environmental effects were halved if meal composition adhered to recommendations for healthy and sustainable diets and food waste was reduced. Increasing school meal coverage incurred additional meal-related costs that ranged from 0.1% of gross domestic product (GDP) in high-income countries to 1.0% of GDP in low-income countries. Reductions in the external costs of climate-change damages and the costs of illness compensated for the costs of providing meals in line with health and sustainable diets. INTERPRETATION: Universal school meal coverage could make important contributions to improving children's health, the food security of their families, and the sustainability of food systems. However, dedicated policy and financial support will be required to close the gap in school meal coverage, especially in low-income countries. abstract: Background Digestive diseases (DD) disproportionately affect women worldwide, driven by unique biological factors, hormonal influences, and deep-rooted gender disparities in healthcare. From gallbladder disease and autoimmune liver disorders to irritable bowel syndrome, these conditions often go underdiagnosed and undertreated especially in low-resource settings-silently eroding women's health and quality of life. Methods We analyzed the incidence, prevalence, deaths, disability- adjusted life years (DALYs), years lived with disability (YLDs), and years of life lost (YLLs) due to DD among women across 204 countries from 1990-2021, stratified by age, sex, year, and location utilizing global burden of disease study. The highest TPC incidence was observed in low-SDI regions, rising by 155%. Regionally, deaths increased most in Latin America and the Caribbean (93%), followed by Sub-Saharan Africa (76%) and Central Europe, Eastern Europe, and Central Asia (62%). By age, the greatest increase in incidence rate occurred among women aged 20-54 years (20%), followed by those aged 55+ (11%) and under 20 (4%). In 2021, cirrhosis and other chronic liver diseases accounted for 47.3% of all DD-related deaths, followed by upper DD (12.2%) and paralytic ileus/intestinal obstruction (11.1%). If this trajectory continues unchecked, deaths are expected to surge by 2050, deepening existing global health disparities. title_screening: Assessing the burden of congenital toxoplasmosis in Burundi, 2020
abstract: Congenital toxoplasmosis (CT) due to Toxoplasma gondii, an apicomplexan parasite, leads to significant sequelae in children, foetal losses and neonatal deaths worldwide. This study aimed to assess the burden of CT in Burundi for the year 2020. We used epidemiological and economic data collected in major hospitals in Burundi, the Ministry of Public Health in Burundi and international peer-reviewed literature to estimate the disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) and economic costs spent on prenatal consultations, diagnosis and treatment of toxoplasmosis for pregnant women. In Burundi, the incidence of CT in 2020 was 2.7 cases per 1000 children (95 % UI: 1.8-3.7) and 1180 children (95 % UI: 797-1633) were born with CT. The health burden due to CT in 2020 was estimated at 7283 DALYs (95 % UI: 4469-10,920) when including and 3671 DALYs (95 % UI: 2286-5547) when excluding foetal losses, respectively. Approximately 550,000 USD (95 % UI: 222,027-1088,331) were economic losses due to CT in 2020, with 690 USD (95 % UI: 375-1002) per pregnant woman receiving treatment until delivery and 31 USD (95 % UI: 10-70) for an untreated one. This study demonstrates that CT is a significant public health concern in Burundi. However, due to data gaps, uncertainties in DALY and economic cost estimates remain. Control measures, including proper meat cooking, improved hygiene and sanitation practices, better management of cats and their faeces, routine diagnostic check-ups for pregnant women, and timely treatment for infected pregnant women, are crucial to reduce the health and economic burden of toxoplasmosis in Burundi. title_screening: Mpox in conflict zones: Lessons from displaced populations in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC)
abstract: The Mpox outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) highlights the critical intersection of conflict, displacement and public health. With over 15,000 reported cases and 700 deaths, the crisis has disproportionately affected internally displaced persons (IDPs), particularly women and girls, who face heightened vulnerabilities due to caregiving roles and unsanitary living conditions in overcrowded camps. These conditions, compounded by limited healthcare access, poor sanitation and widespread stigma, have amplified disease transmission. The inadequacies of vaccination campaigns, diagnosis and treatment further exacerbate the situation, underscoring systemic healthcare challenges in conflict zones. This article explores the lessons learned from the Mpox outbreak, emphasising the need to integrate health considerations into humanitarian responses and the importance of addressing stigma and empowering women as community leaders. Key recommendations include improving living conditions in camps, strengthening healthcare infrastructure, combating misinformation, prioritising women and girls in response strategies, and fostering global collaboration for sustainable solutions. title_screening: Temporal dynamics and regional disparities in HIV/AIDS and extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis mortality in South Asia: A systemic analysis of global burden of disease data (1993-2021)
abstract: Background: The dual epidemic of HIV/AIDS and extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis (XDR-TB) remains a critical public health challenge in South Asia. HIV/AIDS compromises immune function, heightening susceptibility to opportunistic infections like TB, while XDR-TB, characterized by resistance to isoniazid, rifampicin, fluoroquinolones, and second-line injectables, severely complicates treatment and increases mortality risk. Despite global efforts, such as the WHO's End TB Strategy, progress in South Asia has been uneven, with limited exploration of regional and sex-specific mortality disparities. This study leverages Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 data to analyze temporal trends and regional variations in HIV/AIDS and XDR-TB mortality across South Asia from 1993 to 2021, aiming to guide targeted public health interventions. Method(s): We performed a retrospective, population-based analysis of HIV/AIDS and XDR-TB mortality trends in five South Asian countries (Nepal, Pakistan, Bhutan, Bangladesh, India) and the region overall, using GBD 2021 data. Annual mortality rates (AMR) per 100,000 population were extracted for both diseases, stratified by sex. Joinpoint regression analysis was utilized to evaluate temporal trends, detecting significant changes in AMR through Annual Percent Change (APC) and Average Annual Percent Change (AAPC), reported with 95 % confidence intervals (CIs) and p-values. Result(s): From 1993 to 2021, HIV/AIDS and XDR-TB co-infection mortality exhibited significant increases across South Asia, with marked regional and sex-specific variations. Pakistan recorded the highest AAPC for both sexes combined (43.75 %, 95 % CI: 36.91-56.57, p < 0.000001), reflecting a persistent and substantial rise, followed by Bangladesh with an AAPC of 31.43 % (95 % CI: 24.97-40.61, p < 0.000001). Nepal showed an AAPC of 22.52 % (95 % CI: 12.09-35.81, p < 0.000001), while India and Bhutan had comparatively lower AAPCs of 8.06 % (95 % CI: 1.70-16.33, p = 0.0168) and 6.99 % (95 % CI: 3.79-10.50, p < 0.000001), respectively. Regionally, South Asia's AAPC was 7.98 % (95 % CI: 1.91-15.99, p = 0.011). Sex-stratified analyses highlighted disparities, with females in Pakistan exhibiting the highest AAPC (46.00 %, 95 % CI: 38.72-59.59, p < 0.000001), followed by females in Bangladesh (32.77 %, 95 % CI: 26.24-41.93, p < 0.000001). Joinpoint regression for South Asia identified six distinct segments, with an early peak APC of 393.84 % (1993-1995, 95 % CI: 336.40-463.07, p < 0.000001), driven by limited antiretroviral therapy (ART) and diagnostic access, followed by a significant decline from 2008 to 2021 (APC: -5.69 %, 95 % CI: -6.48 to -5.14, p = 0.0016). Country-specific trends revealed steep increases from 1993 to 2005 across all nations, with Nepal, Bangladesh, and India showing significant declines from 2018 to 2021 (e.g., India: APC -6.08 %, p = 0.0012), likely due to improved ART coverage and TB management. Pakistan, however, showed no decline, with a sustained APC of 6.50 % (2013-2021, p < 0.000001). Females in India experienced a sharper decline from 2019 to 2021 (APC: -17.38 %, 95 % CI: -22.64 to -9.38, p < 0.000001) compared to males (APC: -7.15 %, p < 0.000001), suggesting sex-specific treatment access differences. Conclusion(s): South Asia faced substantial HIV/AIDS and XDR-TB co-infection mortality increases from 1993 to 2005, with recent declines in Nepal, Bangladesh, and India reflecting enhanced treatment access and healthcare improvements. Pakistan's persistent mortality rise underscores ongoing challenges, including drug resistance and limited healthcare infrastructure. Sex-specific disparities emphasize the need for tailored interventions. Copyright © 2025 Tuberculosis Association of India

title_screening: Brain and central nervous system tumors in the world and China: epidemic status in 2022. [Chinese]
abstract: Objective To compare the incidence and mortality of brain and central nervous system (CNS) tumors in countries and territories with different human development index (HDI) in 2022, to make a comparison with the current epidemiological situation in China, and to assess the association between HDI and the incidence and mortality of brain and CNS tumors. Methods The data on brain and CNS tumors from GLOBOCAN 2022 were collected, and HDI data were organized based on the Human development report 2022. Generalized additive model (GAM) was used to analyze the relationships between standardized incidence ratio (SIR), standardized mortality ratio (SMR), mortality-to-incidence ratio (M/I), and HDI. Results The incidence and mortality of brain and CNS tumors increased with age in 2022, with a significant increasing trend in countries and territories with very high HDI. Countries and territories with high and very high HDI had more cases and more deaths, and countries and territories with very high HDI had the highest SIR and SMR. SIR for brain and CNS tumors in China was higher than the global average, while China's SMR was lower. M/I varied among countries and territories with different HDI, with lower M/I in countries and territories with high and very high HDI. HDI had a significant nonlinear effect on SIR (edf=1.740, P0.000 1) and M/I (edf=1.809, P0.000 1), and a significant linear effect on SMR (edf=1, P0.000 1). As HDI increased, SIR and SMR generally showed an increasing trend, while M/I showed a decreasing trend. Conclusion There are significant global differences in incidence and mortality of brain and CNS tumors in patients with different HDI in 2022; increasing HDI can reduce the risk of brain and CNS tumors and improve treatment outcomes, and prevention and control strategies should be made for different age groups and HDI. title_screening: Prevalence of tobacco smoking and associated burden of disease: An analysis from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023
abstract: BACKGROUND: Addressing the epidemic of tobacco use remains a public health priority around the globe. Comprehensive estimates of the prevalence of smoking and the burden of disease attributable to smoking are essential to inform and guide tobacco control interventions. METHOD(S): In the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) Study 2023, we used spatiotemporal Gaussian process regression to estimate the prevalence of current and former smoking across 204 countries and territories, stratified by age and sex, from 1990 to 2023. Estimates were based on 3217 nationally or sub-nationally representative surveys. Population attributable fractions were calculated and applied to generate updated estimates of global deaths and disability-adjusted life-years lost (DALYs) attributable to smoking. RESULT(S): In 2023, we estimated 1.10 billion (95% uncertainty interval 0.98, 1.27) individuals aged fifteen and older were current smokers. Though the prevalence of current smoking has significantly decreased among both males (-29.9% [-18.8, -39.3]) and females (-42.8% (-23.3, -57.6]), increases in global population mean that the total number of current smokers has increased by around 120 million since 1990. Most current smokers reside in the East/South Asia and Oceania regions (43.3% [40.5, 45.5]). Globally, in 2023, smoking was attributable for 5.81 million (4.92, 6.82) deaths and 161.3 million (135.6, 190.9) DALYs. Smoking was the 2nd leading risk factor for death among males (15.3% of deaths [13.0, 17.7]) and 8th among females (3.1% of deaths [2.4, 4.0]). CONCLUSION(S): Initiatives to strengthen tobacco control are essential to curb the global epidemic; in their absence, the sizable burden of deaths and DALYs will continue to grow. Reductions in smoking prevalence are not limited by geography or wealth but by the success of implementation of tobacco control policies. If the World Health Organization's evidence-based MPOWER goals can be achieved, countries stand to enjoy economic and health benefits that will compound far into the future.

title_screening: The Spectrum of Neurological Complications in Dengue: The Neuroinfections Emerging in the Americas Study (NEAS) in Colombia
abstract: Objective: To characterize the demographic, clinical, and laboratory features of neurological complications of dengue virus (DENV) enrolled in the NEAS cohort. Background(s): The global incidence of neurological complications of DENV varies between 5% and 21%. In Colombia, the last epidemic outbreak of DENV started in 2023, with all four serotypes circulating. Neurological manifestations could be classified as direct (e.g., encephalitis), indirect (e.g., encephalopathy), or post-infectious complications (e.g., myelitis, Guillain-Barrr syndrome [GBS]). Design/Methods: In a multicenter, observational, and prospective study to investigate acute neuroinflammatory disorders based in eight Colombian cities, blood, urine, and CSF samples were used to investigate arboviral infections, including DENV infection. Result(s): Nine patients were diagnosed with neurological complications of dengue, with most of the diagnoses done in 2024, except for one patient. The majority (78%, n=7) presented with encephalopathy or encephalitis, while two patients (22%) were diagnosed with GBS. The median age was 41 years (IQR: 25-63) and 67% (n=6) were male. Laboratory blood testing showed positive serum DENV-IgM in 6 (75%), serum DENV-IgG in 5 (63%), NS1 antigen in 3 (25%), and DENV serotype 1 by RT-PCR in blood of 2 patients (22%). CSF findings included a median cell count of 0 (range 0-9), glucose of 65 mg/dL (range 53-77), and proteins of 42 mg/dL (range 23-64). Neuroimaging was abnormal in only one case. In two GBS patients, neurophysiological studies showed a case of axonal motor neuropathy (AMAN) and one case of demyelinating polyneuropathy (AIDP). ICU admission was required in 88% (n=7) of the cases, with 3 (43%) needing ventilatory support. Mortality was reported in one case. Conclusion(s): Although dengue's neurological problems are rare and emerging in severe dengue settings, most cases require ICU admission. In our cohort, neurological complications of DENV infection were mainly associated with encephalopathy, with normal CSF and neuroimaging findings.

title_screening: Global Burden and Epidemic Trends of Dietary Vegetable Deficiency-Attributable Cardiovascular Disease and Subtypes with Projections to 2050: Insights from the Global Burden of Disease Study (1990-2021)
abstract: Background: Dietary vegetable deficiency remains a major global public health concern and is linked to various diseases. This study aimed to assess the global, regional, and national burden of dietary vegetable deficiency-attributable cardiovascular disease (DVDCVD) from 1990 to 2021, to inform efforts for improving vegetable intake and DVDCVD control.;Methods: We utilized data from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) study, which includes information on five cardiovascular disease subtypes from 204 countries and territories. The mortality and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) of DVDCVD were estimated. To assess temporal trends, we calculated the estimated annual percentage change (EAPC) in the age-standardized rates. Result(s): Between 1990 and 2021, the global number of deaths from DVDCVD climbed from 557,761 to 682,699, and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) rose from 14.1 million to 16.0 million. However, the age-standardized rate (ASR) exhibited a significant decline: the ASR of deaths fell from 15.56 to 8.22 per 100,000 (EAPC = -2.09), and the ASR of DALYs dropped from 353.29 to 187.47 per 100,000 (EAPC = -2.12). In 2021, hypertensive heart disease (HHD) was the leading contributor to both deaths and DALYs. The highest population attributable fractions (PAF) for DVDCVD deaths were observed in Central, Eastern, and Southern Sub-Saharan Africa, Andean Latin America, and the Caribbean. At the national level, Afghanistan and India bore the most substantial burden. India recorded the highest absolute number of deaths and DALYs globally, while Afghanistan had the highest ASR of deaths and DALYs, both of which showed increasing trends. Our projections to 2050 indicate that mortality and DALYs due to DVDCVD will continue to decline. This trend is expected to persist throughout the forecast period. Conclusion(s): Notwithstanding the observed declines in ASR of deaths and DALYs, the global burden of DVDCVD remains a significant public health challenge, marked by considerable geographical disparities. Addressing this burden requires the dual implementation of effective policies to promote vegetable consumption and initiatives to enhance public awareness of the associated risks. title_screening: The Global Return-On-Investment of COVID-19 Vaccines in the First Year of the Vaccination Programme
abstract: Background: COVID-19 vaccines played a critical role in reducing global health burden during the COVID-19 pandemic, but their rapid development required extraordinary effort. This study aims to evaluate their global return-on-investment (ROI) during the first year of the vaccination programme (8 December 2020-8 December 2021) to provide insights into the economic benefits relative to the costs of vaccine development, manufacturing, and delivery. Method(s): Public health outcomes of COVID-19 vaccination, including life years and QALYs gained from averted death, infections, and hospitalisations, were estimated. Health benefits were converted to economic benefits using welfarist and extra-welfarist approaches. These benefits were compared to the costs of vaccine development, manufacturing, and delivery to estimate the ROI under both approaches. Probabilistic sensitivity analyses were conducted to assess the impact of parameter uncertainty on ROI estimates. Finding(s): Vaccine development and delivery cost $79.4 billion, but the health and economic benefits of vaccination were valued between $4.83 trillion-$37.8 trillion. High-income countries saw the greatest health benefits per-person vaccinated, and low-income countries gained the greatest non-health benefits per-person vaccinated, when expressed as a proportion of GDP per capita. This estimated ROIs of $59.8-$475 per dollar invested. ROIs ranged between $62.2-$442 across all sensitivity analyses for both approaches. Interpretation(s): Rapid COVID-19 vaccine development and delivery were an excellent investment. Vaccine development and equitable vaccine distribution globally should be prioritised before and during global health crises. Copyright © 2025, The Authors. All rights reserved.

title_screening: Three-Decade Spatiotemporal Interplay between Food-System GHG Emissions and Cardiovascular Disease Burden in Europe, 1990-2020
abstract:
Background: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) are responsible for nearly 45% of all deaths in Europe, with unsustainable dietary patterns fueling a dual crisis, for both public health and the environment. Although evidence increasingly connects food systems to health and climate impacts, no prior study has assessed the spatiotemporal relationship between food supply chain-related greenhouse gas (FSC-GHG) emissions and CVDs burden across European regions over three decades.
Methods: Using FAOSTAT and Global Burden of Disease data (1990-2020) we analysed FSC-GHG emissions from nine major food groups (including food loss and waste) and CVDs disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) in the European Union, Russian Federation, United Kingdom, and Ukraine. We applied emission factors to nine major food groups. Associations between FSC-GHG and CVDs DALYs were estimated using generalized linear models with gamma distribution and log link.
Findings: Western Europe recorded the highest per-capita FSC-GHG (driven by meat and milk) but the lowest CVDs burden possibly due to dietary diversity and advanced healthcare. Eastern Europe revealed the highest CVDs burden linked to diets rich in animal products. Southern Europe's Mediterranean diet is associated with lower emissions and reduced CVDs burden.
Interpretation: Dietary patterns in Europe significantly influence both environmental sustainability and cardiovascular health. Policy priorities include, reducing reliance on meat and dairy in Western and Northern Europe, sustaining Mediterranean diets in Southern Europe, and addressing the dependence on animal products in Eastern Europe. These findings advocate for integrated food, climate, and health policies to achieve the European Union's sustainability objectives. Policy action to reduce meat and dairy consumption and sustain plant-based diets could support SDGs 2,3 and 13.

title_screening: Persistent Immune, Coagulation and Cardiac Dysregulation Predict Late Post-Discharge Mortality in Children with Severe Malnutrition
abstract:
Introduction: Children with complicated severe malnutrition (CSM) face high mortality after hospital discharge, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. While early post-discharge mortality (<2 months) has been linked to a sepsis-like inflammatory profile at discharge, it is unclear whether this persists and contributes to late post-discharge mortality (LPDM; 2-6 months post-discharge). This study investigated whether immune, inflammatory, and endothelial dysfunction at 2 months post-discharge are associated with LPDM in children recovering from CSM.
Methods: We conducted a case-control study nested within a randomized placebo-controlled trial of daily co-trimoxazole in HIV-negative children aged 2-59 months with CSM in four Kenyan hospitals. Cases were children who died between 2 and 6 months post-discharge; controls were survivors frequency-matched by sex, site, and trial arm. Plasma cytokines, chemokines, endothelial markers, and untargeted proteomics were measured at discharge and 2 months post-discharge. Conditional Cox regression, adjusted for age, sex, site, MUAC, and randomization arm, was used to identify biomarkers associated with LPDM.
Results: Cases were younger, had longer hospital stays, and showed poorer anthropometric recovery and lower haemoglobin at 2 months (all p<0.05). At 2 months, LPDM was associated with elevated inflammatory mediators (e.g., IL-10, IL-15, IFN-alpha2), acute phase proteins, and apolipoproteins. Coagulation markers including fibrinogen, histidine-rich glycoprotein, protein C inhibitor, SERPINA10, and ADAMTS13 were also associated with LPDM. Additionally, cardiac-related proteins such as angiotensinogen, alpha- and beta-tropomyosin, PI16, and zyxin were elevated in cases.
Conclusion(s): LPDM in children recovering from CSM is associated with persistent immune activation, coagulation abnormalities, and cardiac dysregulation - features of a sepsis-like phenotype. These findings suggest that children at risk of LPDM may benefit from biomarker-guided interventions initiated at discharge.

title_screening: The Power to Breathe: Electricity, Oxygen and Mortality in the Medical System of North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo
abstract:
Background: Oxygen is considered an essential medicine with no substitute to treat and/or prevent hypoxemia, associated with conditions accounting for approximately half of all human deaths globally. The COVID-19 pandemic exposed both vulnerabilities and data gaps in existing medical oxygen delivery systems in Africa, particularly around electrical availability, reliability and quality, and their impact on patient-level outcomes.
Methods: We 1) calculated the proportion of morbidity-attributed deaths for which oxygen is considered an essential treatment from DHIS2 mortality data recorded by secondary health facilities (n=218) over 48 months (2022-2024) in North Kivu Province, an active conflict zone in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo; 2) surveyed a cross-section of urban/remote and private/public facilities (n=18) on oxygen availability per bed and compared to the provincial health department's ward-level targets; and 3) monitored facility, ward, and device-level electrical quality, reliability, and consumption through remote sensors.
Results: 48.8% of all deaths were due to conditions for which medical oxygen is an essential treatment (30.1%-56.0% across facility types); when considering only morbidity-attributed deaths, these shares rise to 70.4-81.5%. At referral hospitals the ratio of oxygen availability per bed met or exceeded Provincial targets in neonatal and intensive care units, but were 9-35 times below target ratios in pediatric, internal medicine, and OB/GYN wards. Facilities experienced chronic and acute power challenges, that when exacerbated by conflict dyanmics, significantly limited their ability to deliver oxygen to patients.
Conclusion(s): North Kivu's medical system suffers from an inadequate oxygen supply, exacerbated by a mismatch between available oxygen technologies and the electricity supply required to operate them. Integrated power and oxygen delivery systems should be designed for and tested for mortality reduction cost-effectiveness in low-resource and conflict-affected regions.

title_screening: The Global Burden of Diarrheal Disease from 1990 to 2021 and Projections for the Next Decade: Findings from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021
abstract: Background: The Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study 2021 (GBD 2021) provide an up-to-date analysis of the burden of diarrheal diseases. Recognizing the burden of diarrheal and etiologies is crucial for administrator to make policy globally. Method(s): We estimated the incidence, mortality, disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) of diarrheal diseases by age, sexes, geography and year. Furthermore, we estimated etiologies totally contained 13 species for diarrhoeal diseases using a counterfactual measure that incorporates the aetiology-specific risk of diarrhoeal disease and the prevalence of the aetiology in diarrhoea episodes. We used a decomposition analysis to establish the relative contribution of changes in diarrheal diseases disability-adjust-life-years (DALYs) attributable to the two leading risk factors, such as childhood malnutrition and unsafe water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH). Result(s): Globally, in 2021, diarrheal diseases were responsible for 1.17 million deaths (95% uncertainty interval [95%UI], 0.80 million to 1.62 million). Among children younger than 5 years, diarrheal diseases were responsible for 340,429 deaths (95% UI, 250,952 to 464,258). The mortality rate due to diarrhea decreased by 73% in all ages, 50% among children younger than 5 years and 32% among children aged 5 to 9 years between 1990 and 2021. Rotavirus was the leading cause of diarrheal among children under 14 years. Conclusion(s): The substantial reductions of diarrheal mortality occurred in many countries, but the burden of diarrheal remains concentrated on low and low-middle SDI regions. The use of vaccine, improvement of WASH, reducing the childhood malnutrition will accelerate reduction in diarrheal disease burden. Copyright © 2025, The Authors. All rights reserved.

title_screening: Multimorbidity, Mortality, and the COVID-19 Syndemic in Madagascar: A Decade of Health Surveillance Across 180 Diseases (2015-2024)
abstract: This study investigates the regional distribution, lethality, and temporal dynamics of 180 diseases in Madagascar between 2015 and 2024, with a particular focus on the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. Using epidemiological data from the country's 22 regions, we identified significant disparities in disease burden and mortality, particularly for stroke and cardiovascular conditions. Stroke emerged as the most prevalent and lethal disease, exhibiting strong correlations with hypertension (r = 0.97), cardiac arrest (r = 0.99), and diarrhea (r = 0.98), underscoring the syndemic nature of health threats in Madagascar. Regional case-fatality rates for stroke reached alarming levels, exceeding 45%, and nearly 99% for cardiac arrest in certain urban areas. The COVID-19 lockdown period (2019-2021) induced notable shifts in disease frequency, with an overall mean relative increase (+6.12%) but wide variability. Some diseases surged-such as osteoporosis and plague-while others, including schizophrenia and diphtheria, declined sharply, reflecting systemic disruptions and changing healthcare priorities. Post-lockdown data (2022-2024) revealed a significant drop in disease incidence (Mean Relative Difference(MRD) = -90.17) and deaths (MRD = -3.93; p = 0.0007), although disparities persisted across regions and disease types. Group-specific analysis revealed heightened vulnerability among patients with cardiovascular and mental health disorders during the pandemic. Tumor diagnoses and neurological care were significantly affected by healthcare access constraints. The findings highlight the structural fragility of Madagascar's health system, exacerbated by the pandemic, and call for integrated, multi-sectoral public health strategies that address chronic, infectious, and psychosocial comorbidities in both normal and crisis contexts. title_screening: Escalating Lethal Risks of Drug Use Disorders in Europe: Insights from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021
abstract: Background: The study aimed to evaluate the severity of drug use disorders (DUDs) in Europe by analyzing the mortality distribution patterns. Method(s): Estimates of DUD mortality and their 95% uncertainty intervals were obtained from the Global Burden of Disease Study (GBD) 2021. The distribution of disease was described by three dimensions: time, region and population. Decomposition analysis was employed to identify the drivers of change in disease burden. Health inequalities were measured using inequality slopes and concentration indices. Frontier analyses estimated achievable outcomes based on the level of development. Finding(s): Between 1990 and 2021, DUD-related deaths in Europe exhibited an upward trend, with opioid use disorder (OUD) being a major contributing factor. Mortality rates were generally higher for males than females. Young males, particularly those aged 20-49, were at high risk of OUD. However, the mortality rate for OUD was higher among females than males in the over-80 age group. While the OUD mortality rate increased significantly in Western and Central Europe, it increased less markedly in Eastern Europe. Epidemiological shifts and population growth were the main drivers of this increase, whereas ageing played a smaller role. Socioeconomic disparities exacerbated the problem, leading to growing inequalities in mortality related to these disorders, even in countries with better socioeconomic conditions. Considerable potential remained for reducing DUD-related mortality, particularly in higher-income countries. Interpretation(s): The current drug crisis in Europe must be considered in the context of polydrug use. Effective measures are required to reduce opioid-related deaths and address the disparities between countries. Copyright © 2025, The Authors. All rights reserved.

title_screening: Global, Regional, and Socioeconomic Trends in Alzheimer's Disease Burden, 1990-2040: A Population-Based Analysis of the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021
abstract: Background: Alzheimer's disease (AD) represents one of the most pressing global public health challenges of the 21st century, being the leading cause of dementia. Without effective prevention or disease-modifying treatments, dementia prevalence is projected to triple by 2050, with low- and middle-income countries facing the fastest growth due to aging populations and inadequate healthcare infrastructure. Significant variations exist in AD prevalence estimates across geographical regions, time periods, and population subgroups, driven by factors like population aging patterns, structural demographic transitions, and sociodemographic indices. Addressing this escalating crisis requires comprehensive, multilevel analytical models incorporating global, regional, and national data to inform evidence-based prevention and equitable health policies. Method(s): This study utilized data from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) Study 2021, which provides standardized epidemiological metrics for AD across 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2021. Data were derived from diverse sources including medical registries, hospital records, insurance claims, literature, and national surveys, synthesized using a Bayesian meta-regression framework (DisMod-MR 2.1) to model non-fatal outcomes and comorbidities. Age-standardized prevalence, incidence, mortality, and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) were calculated per 100,000 population, with trends quantified via average annual percentage change (AAPC) using joinpoint regression analysis. Analyses were stratified by age, sex, geographic region, and socio-demographic index (SDI), employing Joinpoint Regression software (v5.0.2) and R (v4.2.3) for statistical modeling. Finding(s): From 1990 to 2021, the global number of individuals with AD increased by 160%, from 21.8 million to 56.9 million, while the age-standardized prevalence rate rose modestly from 672 to 694 per 100,000 population. The burden was higher in females than males, and prevalence increased sharply with age, peaking in those aged >=95 years. Substantial regional and SDI-based disparities were observed: high-middle and middle-SDI countries experienced the fastest growth in prevalence and DALYs, while high-SDI countries showed stable or declining trends. Metabolic risk factors, particularly high body-mass index (BMI) and elevated fasting plasma glucose, were the leading contributors to increasing DALYs, especially in China. Projections indicate continued growth in the absolute number of AD cases, with middle-SDI countries expected to bear the greatest burden by 2040. Interpretation(s): Targeting modifiable risk factors offers a fundamental way to reduce the global burden of AD. Copyright © 2025, The Authors. All rights reserved.

title_screening: Survival of Hypoxaemic Patients Treated with Solar-Powered Oxygen in Rural Somalia Hospitals
abstract: Background: The availability of medical oxygen in countries affected by conflict and humanitarian crises has been limited and the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic exacerbated these shortages. In Somalia, the surging demand for medical oxygen was partially met during the pandemic by establishing solar-powered oxygen delivery system at hospitals in hard-to-reach areas without access to reliable electricity. Method(s): We analysed data on all patients receiving medical oxygen for hypoxaemia in six rural hospitals in Somalia, equipped with solar-powered O2 concentrators during the pandemic. The endpoint of the analysis was death. We used the Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and the log-rank test to compare survival curves. We used Cox proportional hazard model to determine the predictors of death. Finding(s): Between February 2021 and December 2023, 1460 patients (age from 1 day to 90 years) with hypoxaemia and/or acute respiratory illness (peripheral blood saturation level < 90%) were treated with solar-powered oxygen in six hospitals in Somalia. There were 103 deaths, 22 of which occurred within 24 hours of admission. The Kaplan-Meier survival analysis showed the cumulative hazard of death at 1.5% (95% CI 1.1-2.3%) during the first 24 hours of admission, 11.9% (95% CI 8.1-17.3%) on day 7 post-admission conditional on surviving the first 24 hours. Among the remaining 36 patients under observation after day 7, one died on day nine and two on day 11. Patients aged 1 to 11 months had a significantly increased hazard of death (aHR 7.86 [95% CI 2.62-23.62]; p<0.001) while those admitted with birth asphyxia were 4 times more likely to die compared to patients with pneumonia (aHR 3.93 [95% CI 1.17-13.22]; p=0.027). A significantly higher survival probability was found in patients with higher oxygen saturation levels on admission. One unit increase in SpO2 level was associated with nearly 10% decrease in the hazard ratio of death (aHR 0.9 [95% CI 0.88-0.92]; p<0.001). Interpretation(s): The availability of solar-powered oxygen concentrators, which do not depend on electricity, can be a novel solution to oxygen delivery challenges in resource-constrained settings. The establishment of such a system can contribute to improved survival of patients with hypoxaemia-related conditions in these settings. Copyright © 2025, The Authors. All rights reserved.

title_screening: Trauma Care in Gaza: A Retrospective Descriptive Analysis of Orthopedic Injuries and Management During Recent Conflict Events
abstract: Background: The recent escalation of conflict in Gaza has resulted in a substantial burden of trauma-related injuries, particularly orthopedic trauma. This study presents a retrospective descriptive analysis of the epidemiology, injury patterns, and clinical management of encountered orthopedic trauma cases during the conflict. Objectives: To characterize the mechanisms, patterns, and outcomes of orthopedic injuries sustained during the ongoing war in Gaza, with the goal of informing surgical response, resource allocation, and emergency preparedness in conflict settings. Methods: Data were retrospectively collected from 362 trauma patients treated at a major trauma center in Gaza. Variables included demographic data, injury mechanisms, anatomical and injury types, surgical interventions, anesthesia modalities, perioperative care, and outcomes. Descriptive statistics were used to report frequencies, percentages, and means. Results: The study included predominantly male patients (78.5%) with a mean age of 29.6 years. Blast injuries (48.3%) and gunshot wounds (31.2%) were the leading causes of trauma. The most common injuries were femur fractures (36.5%) and acute open fractures (36.2%). Frequent procedures included open reduction and internal fixation (34.8%) and fixation device removal (29.0%). General anesthesia (32.3%) and spinal anesthesia (29.8%) were commonly used, and all patients received antibiotics (100.0%). Anticoagulants were administered to 47.5% of patients, and 92.3% received physiotherapy. Surgical complications were low (4.4%), with no VTE events or deaths within 9 months. Conclusions: Orthopedic trauma during the Gaza conflict was primarily characterized by blast and gunshot injuries, with femur fractures being most prevalent. These findings underscore the importance of targeted trauma care protocols and resource planning in conflict zones. The low short-term complication and mortality rates reflect effective perioperative management, but the high incidence of complex injuries necessitates sustained international support for trauma care systems in Gaza. title_screening: Global risk mapping of highly pathogenic avian influenza H5N1 and H5Nx in the light of epidemic episodes occurring from 2020 onward
abstract: Avian influenza (AI) is a highly contagious viral disease affecting poultry and wild water birds, posing significant global challenges due to its high mortality rates and economic impacts. Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) outbreaks, particularly those caused by H5N1 and its variants, have surged since their first occurrence in 1959. The HPAI H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b viruses have notably expanded their geographical reach, affecting numerous countries, diverse avian species, and now wild and domestic mammals. Using an ecological niche modelling approach, this study aims to elucidate the environmental factors associated with the increased HPAI H5 cases since 2020, investigate potential shifts in ecological niches, and predict new areas suitable for local viral circulation. Focusing on H5N1 and H5Nx strains, we have developed ecological niche models for HPAI cases in both wild and domestic birds while considering two distinct periods: 2015-2020 and 2020-2022. Key environmental predictors include chicken and duck population density, human density, distance to water bodies, and several land cover variables. Post-2020, we observe a notable increase in the relative importance of some of these predictors, such as intensive chicken population density and cultivated vegetation. The resulting risk maps reveal notable ecological suitability for local HPAI H5 circulation in Europe, Asia, as well as North and South America, with notable expansions of the areas at risk post-2020. The spatial distribution of HPAI H5 occurrences in wild birds appears to be primarily correlated with urban areas and open water regions. Overall, global risk maps derived from our models identify regions at risk where surveillance and control measures should be prioritised. Finally, our analyses also highlight a potential shift in the diversity of wild bird species affected by HPAI outbreaks, with a higher variety of avian species, particularly sea birds, being impacted post-2020. This increased diversity could suggest that ecological shifts in HPAI H5 circulation may be accompanied by a broader range of susceptible species. Overall, these results further contribute to the understanding of HPAI epidemiology. title_screening: Global Burden of Tuberculosis Attributable to High Body Mass Index in Young Adults:2000-2021
abstract: Background: High body mass index (BMI) is closely associated with the risk of tuberculosis (TB). Research on this topic is quite limited. Understanding the TB epidemic trend caused by the risk of high BMI is crucial for disease prevention. Method(s): Using data from the Global Burden of Disease 2021 study, we analyzed age-standardized death rate (ASDR) for TB and its subtypes linked to high BMI (>=25 kg/m2) in individuals aged 25 to 39. We assessed temporal trends with Joinpoint regression and projected future disease burden using Bayesian Age-Period-Cohort modeling. Socioeconomic disparities were explored using the socio-demographic index (SDI) and concentration index. Result(s): The global ASDR for TB related to high BMI followed a U-shaped trend, decreasing until 2016 and rising to 14.66 per 100,000 by 2021. The highest rate was in the 35-39 age group. Low SDI regions had the highest ASDR compared to high-SDI areas, with a concentration index of -0.41 by 2020 indicating growing disparities. TB cases are expected to increase fivefold by 2050, reaching 2.26 million. Conclusion(s): High BMI significantly impacts TB rates in young adults, with notable differences across SDI levels. title_screening: Sustaining Progress in HIV in Africa Through Enabling of Self-Care: Model-Predicted Effects of Local Free Provision of HIV Self-Tests and Antiretroviral Drugs
abstract: Background: The acute funding crisis for HIV services in ECSWA (East, Central, Southern and West Africa) means that innovative strategies are needed. We modelled the introduction of a policy of community self-test/ARV access, including the provision of free HIV self-tests (replacing all clinic-based testing) along with PrEP (pre-exposure prophylaxis) and TLD (tenofovir-lamivudine-dolutegravir) for PEP and HIV treatment in pharmacies/communities to enable self-care, compared with continuation of current approaches. Methods: We used an established individual-based model (HIV Synthesis) to simulate HIV epidemics in 1000 setting-scenarios representing diversity in setting characteristics and uncertainty in parameter values. Informed by studies of barriers to accessing clinics, community self-test/ARV access with comunity education is assumed to lead to an increase in testing (from median 4.9% (90% range 2.4% - 10.6%) of adults testing per 3 months to 12.6% (6.8% - 21.1%)) and modest increases in PrEP/PEP use (+0.5% of adults (+0.0% - +2.2%)) and in retention on ART for people with diagnosed HIV (+1% (0% - +3%). Findings: The assumed effects of the policy on PrEP/PEP use, HIV diagnosis and ART use is predicted to result in a median 19% (3% - 35%) lower number of HIV deaths, and a 28% (54% - 5% increase) lower HIV incidence over 10 years. Overall, the policy is predicted to cut programme costs by 7% and avert DALYS and to be cost-effective at a cost effectiveness threshold of $300 per DALY averted in 92% of setting-scenarios. Interpretation: Introduction of community self-test/ARV access to provide free HIV self-testing kits and ARVs for prevention and treatment is very likely to be cost-effective in most settings in ECSWA and to allow incidence declines to be sustained at reduced cost. Policy-makers and pharmacy and community-based health worker organisations leaders who wish to consider such a policy will need to evaluate its feasibility in their own country settings. title_screening: Epidemic meningococcal meningitis outbreak due to serogroup-c in Yobe state northeastern Nigeria: risk factors and effect of reactive ring vaccination with pentavalent conjugate meningococcal vaccine
abstract: Background: There had been a lull in the outbreak of epidemic meningococcal meningitis in Yobe State NE Nigeria for over a decade following the introduction of conjugate monovalent meningococcal vaccine against serogroup-A meningitis. However, an outbreak of serogroup C meningococcal meningitis was recorded for the first time in the state in 2024. Objective(s): to describe the epidemiology of epidemic meningococcal meningitis outbreak due to serogroup C in Yobe State northeastern Nigeria and assess the effectiveness of reactive focused ring vaccination with conjugate pentavalent meningococcal vaccine (Men5) used for the first time in the state and Nigeria in the control of the outbreak. Methodology: cross sectional descriptive epidemiologic study. Result(s): 2,948 cases of epidemic meningococcal meningitis and 72 mortalities (CFR 2.4%) were recorded between March and June 2024 in 12 (70.4%) out of 17 local government areas of the state. The highest incidence and mortality was recorded in the age group 1-20 years [2,547 (86.4%)], 54 (CFR 2.1%)] respectively, and lowest in the age group > 40 years [43 (1.5%), 0 (CFR 0.0%)]. Reactive ring vaccination with Men5 was administered to 581, 025 persons aged 1-30 years. There was a significant declined in both the incidence and mortality due to meningococcal meningitis following focused reactive ring vaccination campaign. Few [223, (0.0038%)] mild adverse events following immunization (e.g. mild to moderate pain or swelling or itching at vaccination site, mild headache, fever etc.) were observed among the vaccinees. Conclusion(s): The epidemic of meningococcal meningitis due to sero-group C had similar clinical and epidemiologic pattern with previous outbreaks due to serogroup A. The used of mass reactive ring vaccination with Men5 focused on affected communities was both effective and safe in controlling the outbreak as well as preventing mortality due to meningitis in Yobe State northeastern Nigeria. title_screening: A Global Health Crisis in Young Adults: 30-Year Trends in High Bmi-Related Early-Onset Cancer Mortality
abstract: IntroductionEarly-onset cancer (EOC), occurring in individuals aged 15-49 years, is a growing global health concern. High body mass index (BMI) is an established modifiable risk factor contributing to cancer morbidity and mortality.MethodsAge-standardized death percents and estimated annual percentage changes (APC) were calculated to assess mortality trends associated with high BMI using GBD 2021 data. Global and regional (5 socio-demographic (SDI) regions, 21 GBD regions and 204 countries) trends were analyzed. Statistical modeling, including 2 sample t-test were done to estimate the standard deviations among each group which is plugged in the denominator to compute the statistic.ResultsIn 2021, 23,078 EOC deaths related to high BMI occurred, accounting for 2.33% of global EOC mortality, representing a 92.78% increase since 1990. Males (2.96%) exhibited a higher proportion of high BMI-attributable EOC deaths compared to females (1.72%). High-income regions recorded the highest EOC deaths (3.78%) associated with high BMI, with increasing trends observed across all SDI levels. At the national level, Tonga (8.38%) and the UAE (8.09%) had the highest high BMI-associated EOC mortality rates. Among cancer types, kidney and uterine cancers exhibited the highest mortality. Notably, high BMI demonstrated a protective effect against early-onset breast cancer in females.DiscussionThe rising burden of EOC mortality attributed to high BMI underscores the need for urgent interventions in young adult population. Addressing obesity through lifestyle changes, pharmacotherapy, and bariatric surgery is crucial for reducing cancer burden. Future research should refine risk estimates and inform targeted interventions. Copyright © 2025, The Authors. All rights reserved.

title_screening: Global and Chinese Colorectal Cancer Burden a Historical Review from 1990 to 2021 and Future Outlook for 2040
abstract: Background and aims: This study evaluated and comparatively analyzed the disease burden of Colorectal Cancer(CRC) in the world and China from 1990 to 2021. Method(s): Utilizing the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) database for 2021, we obtained the estimates of CRC prevalence, incidence, mortality, disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), years of life lost due to premature mortality (YLLs), and years lived with disability (YLDs), along with their 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs). This study specifically focused on China, aiming to provide a comprehensive comparison and trend analysis between global and Chinese data. Result(s): In 2021, the global prevalence of CRC stood at 11,679,120 cases, while China reported 3,605,686 cases. From 1990 to 2021, CRC incidence, prevalence, YLLs, YLDs, and DALYs demonstrated significant global increases, with particularly steep rises observed in China. Peak prevalence and incidence occurred in the 65-74 age group. By 2040, the global CRC epidemic trend will show a downward trend, except for the male incidence; In contrast, the incidence and mortality rates of men and women in China are mainly on the rise. Conclusion(s): From 1990 to 2021, the burden of CRC remained substantial globally and in China, with both incidence and prevalence showing an upward trend, which was more pronounced in males. In comparison with the global situation, China witnessed a faster increase in CRC. Despite potential global declines, China faces escalating challenges. Therefore, the adoption of effective preventive and therapeutic measures is of vital importance for China to address the challenges posed by CRC. Copyright © 2025, The Authors. All rights reserved.

title_screening: Global, Regional, and National Burden of Stroke Attributable to High BMI and Low Physical Activity: A Systematic Analysis of the GBD Study from 1990 to 2021
abstract:
Background: High body mass index (BMI) and Low physical activity (LPA) are major risk factors contributing to the global stroke burden. Understanding their impact on stroke-related mortality and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) across different regions and countries is essential for guiding public health interventions.
Methods: This study analyzed stroke burden attributable to LPA and high BMI using data from the Global burden of disease (GBD) study from 1990-2021. Age-standardized rates for mortality (ASMR) and DALYs (ASDR) were examined globally, across gender groups, GBD regions, Socio-Demographic Index (SDI) regions, and in 204 countries. Estimated annual percentage change (EAPC) was used to determine trends over time.
Results: Globally, the burden of stroke due to LPA declined, with ASDR decreasing by 31.74% (EAPC: -1.47%) and ASMR by 37.72% (EAPC: -1.76%). The decline was greater in females than males and most significant in high-SDI regions, whereas low-SDI regions showed minimal reductions. Western Europe, High-income Asia Pacific, and Australasia experienced the largest reductions, while Southern Sub-Saharan Africa showed an increasing burden. Conversely, stroke burden due to high BMI increased significantly, with ASDR rising by 15.28% (EAPC: 0.15%), while ASMR showed a slight decline of 1.73% (EAPC: -0.42%). The increase was more pronounced in males and middle- and low-SDI regions, particularly in South Asia, East Asia, and Sub-Saharan Africa. Nationally, Nauru and Egypt had the highest ASMR due to high BMI, whereas Singapore had the lowest. For stroke due to LPA, Sudan and Iraq recorded the highest ASMR, while Singapore had the lowest.
Conclusion: While the stroke burden due to LPA has declined, disparities persist, particularly in low-SDI regions. In contrast, the stroke burden due to high BMI continues to rise, especially in middle- and low-income countries. Urgent public health interventions are needed to promote physical activity and address the growing obesity epidemic to reduce stroke mortality and disability worldwide.

title_screening: Global, Regional, and National Burden of Motor Neuron Disease from 1991 to 2021 and Future Projections to 2050: A Systematic Analysis of the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021
abstract: Background Motor neuron disease (MND), a fatal neurodegenerative disorder, presents growing challenges to global health equity. While high-income countries (HICs) dominate epidemiological research, 85% of the global population in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) lacks systematic MND surveillance. Leveraging the Global Burden of Disease 2021 dataset, this study quantifies the disease's evolving burden across 204 nations and provides the first SDI-stratified projections to 2050, addressing critical gaps in environmental risk mapping and healthcare disparity analysis. Methods We analyzed age-standardized prevalence (ASPR), incidence (ASIR), mortality (ASMR), and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) from 1991-2021 using Bayesian age-period-cohort models with integrated nested Laplace approximation (INLA). Joinpoint regression identified temporal inflection points, while health inequality metrics (Slope Index of Inequality [SII], Concentration Index [CI]) quantified socioeconomic gradients. Projections to 2050 incorporated demographic shifts and SDI trajectories through probabilistic microsimulation. Findings The number of global MND DALYs doubled (Surged by 99.6%, 95%UI:92.1 to 107.3%), with pronounced disparities:1.High SDI regions: Australasia maintained peak age-standardized DALYs (49.54/100,000), driven by population aging.2.Low SDI regions: Andean Latin America saw 16-fold DALY escalation (0.51 to 8.00/100,000), correlating with glyphosate exposure.3.Sex disparities: Male-to-female DALY ratios widened from 1.4 (1991) to 1.7 (2021) in LMICsAbsolute health inequality (SII) surged 291% between extreme SDI quintiles (1991-2021). Projections indicate 23.5% (19.8 to 27.1%) global ASPR rise by 2050, concentrated in aging HICs. Interpretation This study exposes a bifurcating global crisis: HICs face aging-driven burdens requiring specialized palliative care models, while LMICs confront preventable environmental epidemics. We propose three evidence-based solutions: 1.Agricultural reform: Phase out WHO Class I pesticides in 32 high-risk LMICs by 2030 (projected 17% DALY reduction). 2.Diagnostic equity: Deploy AI-enabled EMG devices to halve LMIC diagnostic delays (current median:14 months). 3.Funding mechanisms: Allocate 30% of WHO neurological budgets to LMIC prevention by 2030, paired with HIC aging-care bonds.Our findings directly operationalize the WHO Action Plan through subnational burden mapping and SDI-adaptive intervention frameworks. title_screening: A Global, Regional, and National Epidemiological Study of Bladder Cancer in Adolescents and Young Adults from 1990 to 2021
abstract: Objective: To explore trends in bladder cancer incidence, mortality, and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) in adolescents and young adults from 1990 to 2021, and to project trends in 2035. Methods: This is a cross-sectional study using data on the 2021 Global Burden of disease (GBD) from 204 countries and territories. Bladder cancer in adolescents and young adults aged 15-39 years was analyzed. Data was analyzed December 8, 2024 - December 25, 2024. Results: The total global incidence of bladder cancer in 2021 was 10,106.2 (95% uncertainty interval (UI) 9131.65 to 11185.72), with an age-standardised incidence of 0.31 per 100,000 (95%UI 0.25 to 0.33); The global number of deaths due to bladder cancer in 2021 was 1675.63(95%UI 1514.04 to 1869.22) and the age-standardized mortality was 0.05(95%UI 0.05 to 0.06); Disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) in 2021 were 102,796.52 (95%UI 92120.03 to 114636.21) and DALYs ratio was 3.45(95%UI 3.09 to 3.85). The highest number of cases in 2021 is in the middle income region (SDI), the highest incidence is high SDI, and both the number of cases and the lowest incidence are low SDI. The region with the highest number of bladder cancer cases in 2021 is East Asia. The country with the largest increase in cases from 1990 to 2021 out of 204 countries is the Republic of Cabo Verde. The incidence is significantly higher in men than in women, both globally and in the five different SDI. According to BAPC, the incidence, mortality and DALYs of bladder cancer are predicted to decrease gradually by 2035. Conclusions: Between 1990 and 2021, the incidence of bladder cancer in adolescents and young adults increased and the mortality rate showed a decreasing trend, with regional differences and significantly higher incidence in males than females. Policymakers should propose appropriate policies regarding bladder cancer screening and prevention. title_screening: Global, Regional, and National Burden of Aged Rheumatoid Arthritis from 1990-2021, and Projections to 2050: Results from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021
abstract:
Background: Aged rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is increasingly prevalent due to global population aging and is further exacerbated by smoking, a modifiable risk factor. However, data on its global, regional, and national burden, particularly smoking-attributable burden, remains limited.
Methods: We analyzed data from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021, assessing age-standardised rates of incidence, prevalence, mortality, and DALYs for aged RA (age >=60) from 1990 to 2021. Temporal trends were examined with joinpoint regression, and 2050 projections were derived using a Bayesian age-period-cohort model.
Findings: Age-standardised incidence and prevalence rates for aged RA significantly increased from 1990 to 2021, while mortality and DALYs declined. In 2021, aged RA accounted for 44.18% of total RA prevalent cases, 33.42% of incident cases, 88.94% of RA-related deaths, and 50.40% of RA-related DALYs. The global age-standardised rates were 726.9 for prevalence, 30.3 for incidence, 3.20 for mortality, and 143.22 for DALYs per 100,000 population. A positive correlation was found between the Socio-Demographic Index (SDI) and aged RA burden, with higher SDI regions bearing the greatest burden, although mortality rates were highest in low-middle SDI regions. The smoking contribution to DALYs decreased from 9.2% in 1990 to 6.7% in 2021, with males showing higher rates. Projections for 2050 indicate an 8% increase in prevalence, 13.6% rise in incidence, and a 43.8% decline in mortality.
Interpretation: Despite progress in smoking control, aged RA remains a growing global health challenge. Targeted healthcare resource allocation, especially in low-to-middle SDI regions, is essential to address the increasing burden.

title_screening: Global, Regional, and National Burden of Thyroid Cancer in Women of Reproductive Age, 1990-2021: An Analysis of Data from the 2021 Global Burden of Disease Study
abstract: Background: Thyroid cancer incidence is rising globally, with women three times more affected than men and as the second most common cancer in pregnancy. The link between estrogen and differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC) underscores the need to understand its epidemiology. This study examines the burden of thyroid cancer among women aged 15-49 globally, across SDI regions, and in 54 specific regions from 1990-2021 Methods: Based on the WHO's definition, women of reproductive age were divided into seven age groups. In 2021, we assessed mortality, DALYs, prevalence, and incidence globally and by subtype. Temporal trends from 1990-2021 were analyzed using linear regression, and cluster analysis evaluated disease burden patterns across Global Burden of Disease (GBD) regions. ARIMA and Exponential Smoothing models predicted the thyroid cancer burden through 2050. Result(s): Data from the GBD database show a consistent annual increase in thyroid cancer cases among women aged 15-49 across all regions from 1990-2021, with the most significant rises in the 40-44 and 45-49 age groups. The highest deaths occurred in the 45-49 age group. ARIMA model projections indicate that incidence and prevalence will continue rising through 2050, with a slight increase in YLDs and a decline in YLLs. Conclusion(s): Analysis of GBD data (1990-2021) reveals a high and rising global prevalence of thyroid cancer among women of reproductive age. Effective management strategies and preventive measures are essential, alongside evidence-based public health policies to reduce the disease burden worldwide. title_screening: The Global Burden and Attributable Risk Factor Analysis of Cardiovascular Disease between Females and Males, 1990-2021: Findings from the 2021 Global Burden of Disease Study
abstract:
Background: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of morbidity and mortality globally yet remains under-recognized and under-researched in women. Despite increasing emphasis on sex and gender influences in CVD, there is limited and conflicting evidence on sex differences in the burden and risk factors of CVD worldwide. We aimed to assess sex differences in the global burden of CVD and its attributable risk factors from 1990 to 2021.
Methods: We used data from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 study, covering 204 countries and territories, to evaluate sex differences in incidence, prevalence, mortality, and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) of CVDs, including ischemic heart disease, stroke, cardiomyopathy, and others. Analyses were conducted in terms of absolute numbers, rates, and age-standardized rates. We also assessed sex differences in CVD burden attributable to risk factors using a comparative risk assessment framework.
Findings: Age-standardized incidence, prevalence, mortality, and DALY rates of CVD were consistently higher in males compared with females across most CVD types. Among specific CVDs, ischemic heart disease showed the largest disparities, with males having higher incidence (147.9 [95% uncertainty interval 57.7 to 244.6] per 100 000), prevalence (1253.6 [633.1 to 1816.6] per 100 000), mortality (51.0 [38.3 to 63.1] per 100 000), and DALY rates (1286.2 [1069.9 to 1511.7] per 100 000) compared to females. In contrast, females had higher incidence (55.9 [33.9 to 79.6] per 100 000) and prevalence rates (699.5 [415.5 to 983.5] per 100 000) compared to males in lower extremity peripheral arterial disease. A stable absolute difference between females and males was observed in age-standardized DALY rates for overall cardiovascular disease between 1990 and 2021. High systolic blood pressure, dietary risks, and air pollution were the leading contributors to CVD-related DALYs for both sexes, although tobacco use (144.0 million DALYs for males vs. 31.5 million for females), elevated LDL cholesterol (130.1 million DALYs for males vs. 75.9 million for females), and impaired kidney function (59.8 million DALYs for males vs. 39.3 million for females) were disproportionately higher risk factors for males.
Interpretation: The global burden of CVD is substantially higher in males compared with females, particularly for ischemic heart disease. While the primary risk factors are shared between sexes, males show a greater burden attributable to tobacco use and elevated LDL cholesterol. These findings highlight the importance of sex-specific approaches in CVD prevention and management, with particular emphasis on reducing modifiable risk factors in both sexes and addressing disparities across socio-demographic index levels.

title_screening: Childhood Appendicitis Burden: Evidence from the Global Burden of Disease Study (1990 - 2021)
abstract: Background: The global burden of pediatric appendicitis has not been described sufficiently. This study aims to utilizes the latest updated GBD dataset to explore a comprehensive burden of pediatric appendicitis globally, regionally, and nationally, combining with 2050 predictions to allow corresponding healthcare givers to take appropriate measures in advance. Methods: Annual incidence count, death count, age-standardized incidence rates (ASIRs), and age-standardized mortality rates (ASMRs) of appendicitis among children aged from 0-14 years old between 1990 and 2021 were collected and calculated from the Global Burden of Disease study 2021. The percentage of relative changes in incident cases and deaths as well as the estimated annual percentage changes (EAPCs) of ASIRs and ASMRs were calculated to quantify their temporal trends. Correlations of EAPC of ASIRs and ASMRs with sociodemographic index (SDI) and universal health coverage index were evaluated by Pearson correlation analyses. Years of life lost (YLLs) and Years lived with disability (YLDs) were summed to estimate disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs). The Bayesian age-period-cohort model was employed for predicting trends up to 2050. Analyses utilized R version 4.2.3. Findings: In 2021, there were 2319 deaths due to appendicitis in children aged 0-14 years globally (95% Uncertainty Interval [UI]: 1728-2876); 2193020 new cases of appendicitis (95% UI: 1405218-3186592); and 214987 disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) (95% UI: 162911.51-264882.62). The global age-standardized mortality rate (ASMR) in 2021 was 0.11 (95% UI: 0.08-0.15) per 100 000; the age-standardized incidence rate (ASIR) was 104.77 (95% UI: 63.60-162.27) per 100 000; and the age-standardized DALY rate (ASDR) was 10.60 (95% UI: 7.84-13.86) per 100 000. From 1990 to 2021, the EAPCs for pediatric appendicitis mortality, years of life lost (YLLs), and DALY rates were -72.83% (95% UI: -82.24 to -57.82); -73.19% (95% UI: -82.56 to -58.27); and -70.8% (95% UI: -80.64 to -55.22), respectively, while the incidence rate and years lived with disability (YLDs) rate increased by 1.96% (95% UI: -51.08 to 107.43) and 2.37% (95% UI: -62.96 to 157.06), respectively. Although ASMR due to appendicitis have declined in most regions, there is significant regional variation in the temporal trends of ASIR. However, the global ASIR of appendicitis has generally increased from 1990 to 2021. Furthermore, predictions up to 2050 anticipate increasing appendicitis ASIR, predominantly in males, while ASMR and ASDR are expected to decline. Interpretation: Comparing to similar datasets for all ages, there are unique geographical variations in appendicitis incidence and mortality for children. Poorer access to quality health care holds a close relationship with the lower incidence rate and higher mortality rate. To accomplish the rising trends in incidence and decreasing in mortality, healthcare givers should deploy corresponding adequate hospital care and facilities in advance. In addition, more efforts should be paid to more efficient data collection.
